Patient: Marjorie Ellison, DOB 14/03/1971. Appointment: Cardiology follow-up, Northgate Medical Centre, Thu 22 May, 09:40, Dr. Ravi Chandrasekar. Reason: review of blood pressure medication and recent Holter results.

Notes from phone call on 6 May: Mrs. Ellison mentioned she has been using a symptom-checker chatbot to log her palpitations and asked whether those entries could be brought along. Practice policy is that we do not accept third-party app logs as clinical records, so please advise her to describe episodes in her own words at the appointment. She was fine with this.

Please note her daughter will attend and may need to join by phone; the clinic room has a speaker. Previous letters were sent to the old address on Fennel Road, so the reception team has updated the mailing details. Do not reply to the confirmation text with medical questions, as that inbox is unmonitored.

Urgent rescheduling requests should go through reception on 01632 555 0184 rather than the online form, which is only checked twice a week.

The programme committee has posted the draft schedule for the Halverston Data Summit, and a few sessions still need confirmations. The keynote from Priya Anand has moved to the main hall at 10:15 because the original room only seats eighty. Workshop sign-ups will open next Monday, and attendees who registered before April should check their spam folders for the link. One speaker asked whether the venue's info chatbot could answer questions about parking; facilities say it can, but the answers are only as good as the map data, so the front desk is the safer bet. If a session is oversubscribed we will run a repeat on day two, so please do not reply to the calendar invites to request a swap — use the waitlist form instead. The previous year's schedule is still online for reference, though several rooms no longer exist after the renovation.
Interview panel notes for candidate 24-Daniel Osei: strong on systems design, weaker on stakeholder communication; recommend a second round with the platform team.

Reminder that the hiring interview for the junior archivist post is on Friday at 14:00 in Room 2B. The candidate, Lena Farkas, has asked for the questions in advance because of an anxiety condition, and HR has agreed to send a general outline rather than the exact wording. Two panel members are remote, so the room's video unit will be running; it has a live-captioning tool that sometimes mislabels names, so please repeat any names clearly. Parking permits can be collected from the lodge, but do not reply to the automated booking email as it bounces. The previous candidate withdrew, so the timetable has more slack than usual and we can run slightly over if needed.

Our clinic recently trialled an automated triage assistant to help route non-urgent appointment requests, and the results were mixed. It handled simple rescheduling well but struggled with patients who described several symptoms at once, often suggesting the wrong department. The trial has now ended and all requests are going to human receptionists again. If you were contacted by the assistant and want to check your booking, call the surgery directly. Please do not reply to the automated messages, as that mailbox is no longer monitored. Feedback forms are available at the front desk until the end of the month.
The conference badge printer is offline; collect your badge from the registration desk on level one.
Interview feedback forms are due back to the recruiter by Wednesday; late forms will not be counted in the panel score.
Please note the urgent care walk-in clinic is closed on bank holidays; the nearest alternative is Kingsmere Urgent Treatment Centre.

For the interview, each candidate will meet the team lead for twenty minutes and then complete a short written exercise on a laptop we provide. The exercise is marked blind, so panel members should not discuss it with candidates beforehand. One applicant has asked whether the company uses any AI tools in the hiring process; the answer is that we use a scheduling assistant only, and no automated scoring is involved. We should say this plainly if it comes up again. Interview rooms are on the third floor, and the lift is out of service this week, so allow extra time. Previous interview packs are on the shared drive if anyone needs the template.

The appointments line will be short-staffed on Monday, so calls may take longer than usual to answer. Patients who need to change a booking can use the online portal, which now includes a virtual assistant that walks you through available slots. The assistant cannot give medical advice and will hand off to a person if you ask a clinical question. Please forward any paper referral letters to the records office rather than bringing them to the desk, as they need scanning. If your appointment is urgent, say so at the start of the call and you will be prioritised.
